processing: Orthodox Darjeeling processing, with lighter oxidation in spring as is usual. Sellers describe it as organic, Fair Trade and biodynamic.
harvest_season: Most often seen as spring first flush; as usual in Darjeeling, second flush and later pickings follow.
appearance_dry: Typical of Darjeeling first flush, olive and silvery twisted leaf, darker in later flushes.
appearance_liquor: Pale gold in spring, amber in summer.
appearance_wet: Tender green-and-copper leaf in spring, browner later.
taste_profile: As with other spring Darjeelings, expect a floral, fresh and brisk cup; summer lots are usually rounder and fruitier.

brewing.notes: Western-style for a spring lot. Raise the water to about 90–95°C for second flush.

vintage_note: Sold by year and flush, for example as a dated first flush. Spring lots are best within about a year of picking. Check for the organic and Fair Trade marks and the invoice details.
description:
Selimbong is a Rungbong Valley garden near Pokhriabong. One seller puts it at roughly 1,100 to 1,700 metres with about 153 hectares, and sellers know it for organic and biodynamic growing.

Its processing follows the orthodox Darjeeling pattern, with light oxidation in spring and fuller oxidation later in the year.

A first flush should be floral and fresh, as is typical of spring Darjeeling. Treat it gently, with cooler water, and keep the first steep shorter than you would a standard black tea.

It is easy to mix up with Selim Hill, a different Darjeeling garden. Check the name carefully.
history:
Sellers' accounts credit William Lloyd with founding the garden near Pokhriabong, most often in 1866, though 1886 also appears, so the date is unsettled.

The move to organic farming is dated to 1995, under Tea Promoters India.
